title: Salary & FnF Disputes in India: 2026 Data Report
h1: Salary and FnF Disputes After the Code on Wages: First-Year Data
metaTitle: Salary & FnF Disputes in India: 2026 Data Report
metaDescription: Data report on unpaid salary and FnF disputes under the Code on Wages: statutory turnaround times, dispute causes, and legal notice recovery.

sectors.name: Information Technology & Software Services

sectors.regulator: State Labour Commissioner / Code on Wages Authority

sectors.name: Startups & High-Growth Tech Enterprises
sectors.primaryCause: Runway cash constraints, unvested ESOP clawbacks & sudden restructuring
sectors.regulator: Ministry of Labour & Employment / NCLT Section 9

sectors.name: BFSI & FinTech Entities

sectors.regulator: State Labour Commissioner / Payment of Gratuity Authority

sectors.name: Retail, E-Commerce & Supply Chain Logistics

sectors.name: Healthcare, Diagnostics & Pharmaceuticals

disputeCauses.cause: Notice Period Buyout & Resignation Timing Conflict
disputeCauses.legalStatus: Employer cannot withhold earned wages for unserved notice unless contractually quantified, and total deductions must not exceed 50% under Section 18(3).

disputeCauses.cause: Arbitrary Asset Return & IT Clearance Delays
disputeCauses.legalStatus: Holding entire FnF for uninspected laptops is unlawful; deductions require itemized appraisal and employee opportunity to respond.
Wages definition under Section 2(y) includes remuneration expressed in terms of money; confirmed target bonuses constitute legally enforceable wages.
Section 7(3A) of Gratuity Act mandates simple interest on delayed payment after 30 days; 4 years 240 days fulfills 5-year eligibility.

methodology.sampleFrame: Aggregated intake and post-dispatch resolution case registry of LegalRecovery.in across employee claims initiated post-launch on May 25, 2026. Awaiting compilation.
inclusionCriteria: White-collar and blue-collar employment separation disputes with verified offer letters or employment agreements.
Documented Last Working Day (LWD) and written resignation or termination notices.
Clear wage default exceeding the Section 17(2) two-working-day statutory threshold.
Advocate demand notice served with Proof of Delivery to company directors or registered office.
exclusionCriteria: Informal gig economy disputes without proof of master-servant contractual relationship.
Claims barred by limitation or where an active arbitral tribunal is already seized of the matter.
Unquantified bonus claims dependent entirely on future subjective promoter discretion.

definitions.preNoticeDelay: Calendar days elapsed between employee's Last Working Day and advocate notice service.
definitions.postNoticeResolution: Business days between notice delivery and receipt of cleared bank remittance.
definitions.noticeResolutionRate: Percentage of wage claims resolved pre-litigation without requiring Labour Court proceedings.

methodology.dataIntegrity: Strict empirical protocol: LegalRecovery commenced operations on May 25, 2026. In accordance with rigorous research standards, no estimated or pre-launch figures are published. The 2026 cohort dataset is under active compilation.
